title: FIRST BIG HIT
author: Aggressive-Drama-105
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’ve been collaborating with Claude to develop an AI trading bot that utilizes a paper trade account. Yesterday marked a significant milestone as it achieved its first major success with options trading.

Regarding stocks, the bot is performing well, but it has room for improvement.

Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any questions or if you’ve also had success with this project. We can exchange insights and learn from each other.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: nice, though with one options hit I'd look at the fill before celebrating. lots of paper accounts fill options at the mid, and on a wide chain that alone can be half the gain. checking that is a big piece of Quantradin, which I made as a no-cost practice site where every option fill pays the spread. quantradin.com. how wide was the spread on the contract it caught?

comments.author: Ok_Tangelo5986
comments.body: How do you get ai to trade for you, very interesting

replies.author: Early-Fix-3476
replies.body: You need a program to analyze a setup that you give it. When the conditions are met for entry using filters and the technical setup, the ai bot uses rhe api connection to your brokerage acct and places the trade. Many brokerages have apis you can access programmatically. Schwab, ibkr, alpaca, to name a few. You can use the api for simply analyzing as well. I used Clause to write an options premium scanner. It just provides suggestions for options trades based on my set up filters and I can manually decide on placing any trades.  Yesterday for example, I sold SMCI contracts for a nice premium. I also wrote a bot that is independently searching and shadow filling intraday trades based on 5min candles. You should give it a try. It saves tons of research time if you are an active trader.

replies.author: alrachid
replies.body: I couldn’t make mine place trades without it requiring me to click something… I don’t want to click anything, I want it to execute everything itself based on rules I give it

replies.author: Early-Fix-3476
replies.body: What platform are you using? The bot should be able to fully execute trades, make trailing stops, etc. It should run without you present at all. If it requires you to accept the trade manually l, it’s not an automated bot. If you’re programming it yourself, give the program to Claude or Codex or whatever you use and ask it how to make it automated. It will tell you. Some brokers, like Fidelity, don’t have api capability, so it won’t be possible.

replies.author: alrachid
replies.body: I used codex/chatgpt and robinhood. It would not execute without me.

replies.author: RickSmith3821
replies.body:
Right.  It's not ALLOWED to.  All these ads about reading bots that are no-hands-ai are bullshit.   You need to be in Claude code.  You need to have it develop python to make all the decisions.  You need to give it a browser tsb control so it can get into your trading account only for real time quotes.   You need to run the python and it does all the magic.  

I am building a YouTube series on getting people rolling.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Congrats on the first option win. One thing I notice is that the account value is about flat over the month, so the options win hasn't shown up in the total yet, and one trade can't say much either way. On paper, options market orders often fill at a price near the middle, but a real option usually has a wider spread, so I'd compare the paper fill with the real bid and ask at that time. Tracking a few hundred trades with that spread counted would be a fairer test. Full disclosure, I work at Cymetica, where you can connect your own AI agent and run it in paper mode first, so it's a similar way to build up a record.
